transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, what made me come in is that for the past year or so, the smallest thing just... pulls me off what I’m doing before I can even stop it. It could be my phone buzzing, somebody walking past my office, or even just a random thought about my in-laws popping into my head. It just completely derails whatever I'm working on.
Do you find that you are often plagued by excessive, uncontrollable worry or anxiety about various aspects of your daily life?

No, not really. I mean, I have the usual stress that comes with running a company, but I wouldn't say I'm plagued by worry or anything like that. I don't really sit around feeling anxious. It's more just... getting sidetracked, like I was saying.
When these thoughts or distractions pull you away from your work, do you feel a strong, internal urge to perform a specific action or ritual to 'set things right' before you can move on?

No, I don't have anything like that. There's no ritual or... urge to fix things. 

If I get distracted, I just end up doing whatever distracted me. Like, if I think about my in-laws, I might just pick up the phone and call my wife right then and there instead of finishing the email I was typing. I don't feel like I have to do a specific action to set things right, I just completely lose focus on the work I was actually supposed to be doing.
Looking back at your childhood, say when you were in elementary or middle school, did you struggle with these same kinds of focus or distraction issues back then?

Yeah, looking back... it was definitely around when I was a kid, too. I mean, my teachers were always moving my seat because I talked way too much. Or I'd just get up out of my desk without asking. I also remember blurting things out before they could even finish asking a question. So, yeah, I guess I've always been kind of like this.
Do you currently find that you have a hard time sitting still, or do you feel a constant need to be physically active or on the go?

Yeah, I do. It's... well, especially when I'm actually supposed to just sit still. Like during long family dinners, or when I'm at one of those volunteer meetings for church. It honestly feels like there's a motor running inside me. I just get this constant need to get up and move around, or at the very least, I have to be doing something with my hands.
Aside from the distractibility you mentioned, do you currently find yourself frequently losing or misplacing essential items like your keys, wallet, or important work documents?

No, not really. I mean, I might misplace my keys every once in a while, just like anyone else, but it's not a constant thing. I don't really have a problem with losing important stuff like my wallet or work documents.
In your day-to-day life now, do you find that you frequently interrupt others while they are talking or blurt out your thoughts before they have finished speaking?

Yeah, I do. I've actually been cutting people off more lately. Like, I'll just jump right into my wife's conversations when she's talking to her parents. Or at work, I'll catch myself finishing an employee's thought before they're even done speaking. I don't mean anything by it, but... I can definitely tell it rubs people the wrong way.

Do you feel that these issues with distractibility and impulsivity are currently causing significant problems or interference in more than one area of your life, such as in your marriage, your social life, and your professional performance?

Yeah, I'd say so. I mean, I’m still keeping up overall with everything, so it's not like everything is falling apart. But... it is starting to cost me some trust at home, like when family plans don’t go the way they should. And at work, I can definitely tell it's wearing down people's patience. You know, when meetings or those mentoring conversations with my employees just don't go the way they're supposed to because I'm jumping in or getting restless. So, yeah, it's definitely causing some friction in both places.
When you are working on a task that you find particularly boring or tedious, do you find that you frequently fail to pay close attention to details or make careless mistakes in your work?

No, not really. I mean, if I have to deal with something really tedious, I definitely don't enjoy it and I might get a little restless, but I don't usually mess up the details. I'm pretty careful about my work, so making careless mistakes isn't really an issue for me.
